desks.Dividends: Microsoft, ex Thu Nov 19 at $0.98 per quarter (pay Dec 10), is the only declared watchlist ex-date in the window, its 24th consecutive annual increase, and the last purchase day for entitlement is Wed Nov 18. Apple's dividend is still undeclared, with a Monday Nov 9 date pattern-plausible from the Feb 9, May 11 and Aug 10 cadence but UNVERIFIED until declared, and third-party Nov 10 listings are projections, not declarations. Nvidia's next declaration normally accompanies its Nov 17 earnings, pointing to an early-December ex-date outside the window. SPY and QQQ point to mid-December on pattern only, Tesla pays no dividend, and no cuts or specials were found among watchlist names.
desks.Earnings: Apple reports Mon Nov 2 after close (results about 1:30 p.m. PT, call 2:00 p.m. PT) with an options-implied move of about 4.25% from the live Nov 4 straddle, against a reported typical move of about 2% over the past eight quarters. Consensus revenue is $112.95 billion and EPS $1.98, against company guidance as reported of 9-11% revenue growth and a 47-48% gross margin, so the December-quarter guide is the bar, not the September print. Microsoft reported Oct 28 and Tesla reported Oct 21. Nvidia reports Tue Nov 17 after close, company-confirmed, outside this window.
desks.Futures: Hormuz is a two-way weekend binary into Monday's open: a new Oct 31 tanker incident and a live Doha mediation track with a reported two-day reopening proposal, against a post-midterm US strike decision still pending, while Hormuz transits in the week ending Oct 28 ran about 70% below pre-war levels. Crude settled Fri Oct 30 with Dec Brent expiring at $117.64, Jan Brent at $113.43 and WTI at $104.12; the $4.21 Brent gap is the Dec-to-Jan roll, not a selloff. Natural gas is the counterweight, with Dec Henry Hub near $2.90 and winter and summer-2027 strips at five-year lows into a warm NOAA outlook for Nov 5-11. Next catalysts in order: OPEC+ Sun Nov 1, midterms Tue Nov 3, EIA petroleum Wed Nov 4, EIA gas Thu Nov 5, jobs Fri Nov 6, WASDE and the Short-Term Energy Outlook Tue Nov 10. Dec corn held at $4.47 3/4, a four-month low.
desks.Parity: No published put-call or box parity violation was found for the watchlist this week. The new headline-index item is Okta joining the S&P 500 before the open Wed Nov 4, replacing Kenvue, which Kimberly-Clark is acquiring; Glaukos replaces Okta in the MidCap 400 and McGrath RentCorp replaces Glaukos in the SmallCap 600. Watch for index-fund rebalancing flow in Okta and Kenvue around the Nov 4 open, not for a SPY parity break, since a single-name acquisition-driven swap does not change box or put-call math. The S&P style-index methodology overhaul, effective before the open Dec 21 with pro-forma files Dec 4, is unchanged since yesterday, and the Nasdaq-100 Fast Entry proposal from Feb 2026 remains unadopted as far as this sweep found.
desks.Premium: Apple's Nov 4 expiry at 47.2% implied volatility against 14.9% trailing realized volatility is event pricing ahead of the Nov 2 print, not a mispricing signal, and premium into the binary is to be avoided. Nvidia's Nov 20 expiry at 48.7% is event pricing into its Nov 17 earnings, while its front expiries are ordinary. SPY has no clean implied-versus-realized verdict: Friday's move drives 32.2% of the fresh 20-day window's variance, over the 30% line, so the read is WINDOW-CONTINGENT, and QQQ sits just under the line at 29.8%. Tesla's front implied volatility of 33.4% sits below its 36.9% trailing realized level, a fact about the two prints, not a cheap call. SPY's call-put implied volatility spread of 4.2 points is the widest on the board, so its 12.6% mean is approximate. Implied-volatility rank is UNVERIFIED for all six names.
desks.Quant lab: Nine new candidates were appended to the ledger as rows 188-196, with no TEST and no INTEGRATE movement this run. The strongest is the MIDAS-EPU volatility-forecast study (score 58, WATCH), valued for its honest documentation that the EPU correction lowers QLIKE against XGBoost controls on all three markets but raises MSE and does not improve CSI300 interval quality, a caution for any volatility-forecast comparison, not an adoption. The zero-shot time-series foundation-model commodity-futures benchmark (score 55, WATCH) is the first foundation-model benchmark in the futures desk's lane. The only TEST candidate remains number 171, with sandbox follow-up owned by the weekly job.

headline: Daily research brief — Saturday, October 31

items.detail: Apple reports Mon Nov 2 after close, with consensus revenue of $112.95 billion and EPS of $1.98, and the Nov 4 expiry straddle implies a move of about 4.25%, roughly double the reported typical move of about 2% over the past eight quarters. Front implied volatility of 47.2% is about 3.2 times trailing realized volatility of 14.9%. The swing factor is the December-quarter guide, against company guidance as reported of 9-11% revenue growth, plus the first call under the new chief executive and a tariff-refund margin benefit, not the September quarter itself. That combination argues against paying premium into the print. Nvidia on Tue Nov 17 is the next binary, with Nov 20 implied volatility at 48.7%.
items.title: Apple Nov 2 is the week's binary event, and premium into it is event pricing

items.detail: A further tanker incident in the Strait of Hormuz was reported Sat Oct 31, near the Iranian island of Lavan, while Iranian negotiators met Qatari mediators in Doha after talks in Tehran, with a reported proposal cutting the implementation period of a Hormuz-reopening plan to two days. That proposal is single-sourced in part and unconfirmed by US or Iranian officials, and attribution for the Oct 30-31 incidents is unestablished in sourced reporting, so no deal is treated as done. The hardest physical datapoint is the transit count: Hormuz transits in the week ending Oct 28 ran about 70% below pre-war levels. Crude settled Fri Oct 30 with Dec Brent expiring at $117.64, Jan Brent at $113.43 and WTI at $104.12, so the $4.21 Brent gap is the Dec-to-Jan roll, not a selloff. Monday's open reprices on whichever weekend signal hardens first, a deal or a post-midterm strike decision.
items.title: Hormuz is now a two-way weekend binary, not just a risk premium

items.detail: Settled Fri Oct 30 closes put SPY at $755.72, down 1.77% on the day, QQQ at $690.49, down 3.47%, and Nvidia at $204.64, down 4.22%, with growth and QQQ beta leading down. Outside Apple, front implied volatility sits at or below trailing realized volatility for QQQ, Nvidia and Tesla, and modestly above it for Microsoft, so there is no broad volatility edge in either direction. One caution blocks a clean SPY verdict: Friday's move drives 32.2% of the fresh 20-day window's variance, over the 30% line, making any SPY implied-versus-realized read WINDOW-CONTINGENT, and QQQ at 29.8% sits just under the line. All quotes here are Friday-close marks pulled Saturday, not live Saturday prints, and Monday's open can gap away from these strikes.
items.title: A hard growth selloff, but SPY has no clean volatility verdict

items.detail: FRED prints dated Thu Oct 29, the latest in the pull, put the effective fed funds rate at 3.88%, inside the 3.75-4.00% target range held at the Oct 28 FOMC decision, the 2-year at 4.61% and the 10-year at 4.98%, a 2s10s spread of +37 basis points after widening 6 points on the week. SOFR at 3.94% sits 6 basis points over the effective fed funds rate, a normal overnight funding print with no stress signal. The 10-year is off its 5.31% Oct 5 high, but near 5% it remains a valuation headwind for long-duration names on discount-rate grounds, and the curve gives no inversion signal to offset that read. Rates are a steady headwind here, not a catalyst, and Fri Oct 30 FRED observations had not yet landed at run time.
items.title: Rates: 10-year at 4.98%, curve sloping up, funding calm
